pairs.why: B sits a little farther back with milder perspective and a clearer receding track, closer to the real cards' moderate high three-quarter view, while A's nose-in framing is tighter and more forced.
Both use the same low, wide horizon view with sea and beach layers, unlike the real card's tight high-angle close-up, so this vector doesn't separate them.
B is tilted a bit more so the top face and the sole's rim thickness show, like the real high three-quarter camera, but the difference is slight.
A's boot shows the opening from slightly above and sits on the ground with a three-quarter turn, like the real objects' high camera, while B is a flat side profile that floats.
A shows the glass rim ellipse from a slightly high camera over a table plane like the real card, while B reads lower and flatter with less top face.
A keeps the real card's mild high tilt with the earbuds small and on the same plane, while B's big earbuds in the foreground give a wide-angle, forced perspective.
A shows the foot pockets and blades from a high three-quarter camera with mild foreshortening like the real fins, while B's pockets read more frontal and lower.
Both have the same frontal shelf, panel and wall layering with a similar tilted target, so the camera and depth give no reason to choose.
